_comment: Experimental bands the campaign monitor compares live results against.
PROVENANCE MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBERS HERE.  These are the EUROFER97
neutron values for T <= 400 C used through the 2026-07-31 anchor campaign.
They are NOT the frozen Table G.36 fits that targets.yaml is meant to carry
verbatim for calibration - this file exists so the monitor can tell you
'the ensemble is nowhere near the data' while runs are still going, not to
define the likelihood.  Tier 4 must use the real target file.
f_100 must be compared in the TEM-FILTERED convention.  Number- and
content-weighted conventions differ by a factor of 2 on one and the same
run (0.824 vs 0.408), which is larger than the effect of any conversion
parameter inside its prior - so comparing the wrong one is worse than not
comparing at all.  run_ensemble emits f_100_tem at four cutoffs; the
monitor watches the 1.0 nm one because that is the middle of the reported

SWELLING WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 (author): in F/M steels it is small and not a target the campaign must reproduce, AND it is N_voids x mean_n_v exactly - a deterministic function of two other observables, so including it double-counts the void channel in a variance decomposition. Still emitted as a health check, never screened or calibrated on.

N_loops_100.note: median of the EUROFER97 <100> loop densities

d_100_nm.note: median 7.9; the full reported range is very wide (2.8-180)

f_100_tem_1.note: TEM-filtered at d_min = 1.0 nm. <100> is the MAJORITY character at 300-400 C - the opposite of what the pre-2026-07-31 priors assumed

N_loops_111.note: no clean target isolated yet; watched because f_100 is dominated by it

N_voids.note: cavity density; He-dependent, so it needs a per-condition target

d_cavity_nm.note: cavity diameter d = 2(3 m Omega/4 pi)^(1/3). Added 2026-08-02 when swelling was withdrawn, so the void channel keeps size information and is not density-only. No clean EUROFER target isolated yet - it is He-dependent and needs a per-condition value.

mean_n_v.note: mean cavity size in vacancies; the size half of the void channel
